definitions.explanation: The quality of being sweet in taste. Used especially in food and cooking contexts when discussing the sweet element of a flavor profile.
A sweet food item, especially traditional Japanese sweets and desserts. Used as a general term for sweets in food culture contexts.

examples.japanese: このトマトは{甘味|かんみ}が{強|つよ}い。
examples.english: This tomato has a strong sweetness.

examples.japanese: {塩|しお}を{少|すこ}し{加|くわ}えると{甘味|かんみ}が{引|ひ}き{立|た}つ。
examples.english: Adding a little salt brings out the sweetness.

examples.japanese: {甘味|かんみ}{料|りょう}を{使|つか}わずに{果物|くだもの}の{自然|しぜん}な{甘味|かんみ}だけで{仕上|しあ}げたジャムです。
examples.english: This is a jam finished using only the natural sweetness of the fruit, without any sweeteners.

examples.japanese: {食後|しょくご}に{甘味|かんみ}はいかがですか。
examples.english: Would you like a dessert after your meal?

examples.japanese: この{甘味|かんみ}{処|どころ}は{抹茶|まっちゃ}パフェが{人気|にんき}だ。
examples.english: This sweets shop is popular for its matcha parfait.

examples.japanese: {京都|きょうと}には{老舗|しにせ}の{甘味|かんみ}{処|どころ}がたくさんあり、{観光客|かんこうきゃく}に{人気|にんき}のスポットになっている。
examples.english: Kyoto has many long-established sweets shops, which have become popular spots for tourists.

notes:
READING NOTE:
The same kanji {甘味|あまみ} can also be read あまみ, which means sweetness as a taste quality. The reading かんみ covers both the taste quality (sense 1) and the food item (sense 2), while あまみ is limited to the taste quality only.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {甘味|かんみ}が{強|つよ}い (strong sweetness)
- {甘味|かんみ}{料|りょう} (sweetener)
- {甘味|かんみ}{処|どころ} (Japanese sweets shop)
- {甘味|かんみ}を{楽|たの}しむ (enjoy sweets)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {甘|あま}さ: sweetness (general, can be abstract — sweetness of life, etc.)
- お{菓子|かし}: snacks, sweets (broader category including Western and Japanese sweets)
- {和菓子|わがし}: Japanese sweets (specifically traditional Japanese confections)
